hints: Focus on what the two numbers in $^{70}_{32}\text{Ge}$ really tell you, protons from the bottom number and neutrons from the difference.
Work out Ge first: it has 32 protons and 32 electrons, with $70 - 32 = 38$ neutrons to compare against.
Remember a 2+ ion has lost 2 electrons, then check each statement for electrons, neutrons and protons in turn.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Ge atom**

Great start, let us read the symbol carefully. The lower number is proton number, the upper number is nucleon number.

$$^{70}_{32}\text{Ge}: \text{protons} = 32, \text{neutrons} = 70-32 = 38, \text{electrons} = 32$$

**Check statement 1 for electrons**

Selenium has proton number 34, so a neutral Se atom has 34 electrons. A $\text{Se}^{2+}$ ion has lost 2 electrons.

$$\text{electrons in }^{79}_{34}\text{Se}^{2+} = 34 - 2 = 32$$
This matches the 32 electrons in Ge, so statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 for neutrons**

Neutrons are always nucleon number minus proton number. Apply this to zinc.

$$\text{neutrons in }^{68}_{30}\text{Zn} = 68 - 30 = 38$$
This matches the 38 neutrons in Ge, so statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 for protons**

Protons are simply the lower number. Gadolinium has 64 protons.

$$\text{half of 64} = 32$$
This matches the 32 protons in Ge, so statement 3 is correct. All three are correct.

options.A: Correct, because statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true. Ge has 32 electrons matching Se2+, 38 neutrons matching Zn, and 32 protons which is half of 64 in Gd.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination (1 and 2 only) misses that statement 3 is also true, since half of 64 protons in Gd is exactly 32, the proton number of Ge.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination (2 and 3 only) wrongly leaves out statement 1. Many students forget to subtract electrons for a positive ion, but 34 minus 2 is 32, so it does match.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination (1 only) is far too narrow. Both the neutron calculation for Zn (68 minus 30 is 38) and the proton halving for Gd are also correct.
